asker_query: Doctor, I keep sighing and gasping every few minutes. My chest feels empty. My saturation is 92, my wife says I look normal. Since my friend Antonio died last week I cannot stop thinking about it. Am I dying? Is this the end?
answer:
It is completely understandable that you are feeling frightened; breathlessness is a very distressing sensation, and it is common for it to worsen during times of grief or emotional turmoil. In the context of advanced COPD, breathlessness is often a subjective experience that can occur even when oxygen levels are stable. To manage this, we must first address the "correctable" contributors, such as ensuring your inhaler technique is optimal and checking for any underlying respiratory infections or fluid buildup. While your current medications (Tiotropium and Budesonide-Formoterol) are standard, the "air hunger" you describe—especially when linked to anxiety—often responds well to non-pharmacological techniques. You should continue your prescribed inhalers as directed, but please consult your palliative care team to discuss if a low-dose, short-acting anxiolytic or a specific adjustment to your respiratory management is appropriate to help you feel more at ease.
For your immediate comfort at home, focus on positioning and breathing retraining. When you feel an episode of gasping or panic, sit upright and lean forward, which helps your respiratory muscles work more efficiently. Practice "pursed-lip breathing"—inhaling slowly through your nose and exhaling through pursed lips as if blowing out a candle. Your wife plays a vital role here: she should remain calm, speak in a soothing voice, and reassure you that while the sensation of breathlessness is terrifying, you have recovered from these episodes before and will do so again. Avoid the urge to rush or over-exert yourself; pace your activities throughout the day. If you find your anxiety is overwhelming, it is essential to discuss this openly with your family and your palliative care provider, as addressing these fears is just as important as managing your physical symptoms.
